plan.summary: Automatically triage new unassigned bug reports in the GitHub repo by requesting reproduction details and marking them as needing info.

values.name: Triage comment

steps.label: Discover open unassigned bug issues

steps.label: For each bug issue, post triage comment and label

plan.name: github-stale-pr-nudge
plan.title: GitHub stale PR review reminder
plan.description: Finds open pull requests in a GitHub repository that have been awaiting review for more than 2 days and posts a gentle reminder comment on each one.
plan.summary: Automatically nudge reviewers on stale PRs that need attention.
plan.generalization: The recording processed a single PR, but the automation generalizes to iterate over ALL open PRs in the target repository that have been created more than 2 days ago and are still awaiting review. For each matching PR, it posts a reminder comment with the reviewer tagged.

steps.label: Query stale PRs awaiting review
steps.prompt: Use the GitHub CLI (gh pr list) to find all open pull requests in the {{repo}} repository that were created more than {{stale_days}} days ago and are currently awaiting review. Calculate the cutoff date as today minus {{stale_days}} days (in ISO format YYYY-MM-DD for the gh search query). Return the PR numbers and their metadata.

steps.label: Post reminder comments on each stale PR
steps.prompt: For each PR returned from the previous step, use gh pr comment to post a friendly reminder comment on that PR asking the reviewer to take a look. Include a message like: 'Friendly ping — this PR has been waiting on review for a couple of days, could you take a look?' Post to the {{repo}} repository.

plan.name: acme-pricing-tracker
plan.title: Acme Pricing Tracker
plan.description: Fetch the Pro plan's monthly and annual prices from the Acme pricing page and update a budget spreadsheet with the latest figures. Runs daily to track pricing changes.
plan.summary: Monitors the Acme pricing page daily, extracts the Pro plan's monthly ($49) and annual ($490) prices, and records them in the budget spreadsheet.
plan.generalization: The recording captured fetching current prices from a public pricing URL and writing them to a local spreadsheet. The automation generalizes by: (1) fetching the pricing page content on every run, (2) extracting the Pro plan prices dynamically from the HTML, and (3) updating the budget sheet with those current values—handling any price changes automatically.

steps.label: Fetch the Acme pricing page
steps.prompt: Use web_fetch to read the Acme pricing page at {{pricing_url}} and extract the Pro plan's monthly price (e.g., '$49 / month') and annual price (e.g., '$490 / year'). Parse the HTML to find these price strings.

steps.label: Update the budget spreadsheet
steps.prompt: Open the budget spreadsheet at {{budget_file}} using the xlsx skill. Locate the cells for the Pro plan's monthly and annual prices and update them with the values fetched in the previous step. Save the file.

plan.name: acme-invoices-extract
plan.title: Extract Acme Books invoices
plan.description: Fetches the latest invoice rows from the Acme Books invoices page and appends them to a tracking spreadsheet. Runs daily at 9am to capture new invoices.
plan.summary: Daily automation that extracts all invoices from the Acme Books web page (id, customer, amount) and records them in a spreadsheet, skipping any already present.
plan.generalization: The recording showed copying 3 invoice rows from a web page into a spreadsheet. The automation generalizes this to: (1) fetch the current invoices page each run, (2) extract all invoice rows as structured data, (3) append only new invoices to the tracking spreadsheet (by checking for duplicates by invoice id). This handles any number of invoices and detects new ones across runs.

steps.label: Fetch invoices from the web page
steps.prompt: Use web_fetch to retrieve the invoices page from {{invoices_url}}. Parse the page and extract all invoice rows with their id, customer name, and amount. Store these as a structured list.

steps.label: Load the tracking spreadsheet
steps.prompt: Use the xlsx skill to read the spreadsheet at {{tracking_file}}. Identify the invoice id column and note which invoices are already recorded.

steps.label: Append new invoices
steps.prompt: Compare the fetched invoices with the spreadsheet. For each invoice not already present (by invoice id), append a new row to the spreadsheet with the id, customer, and amount. Use the xlsx skill to save the updated spreadsheet.

plan.name: research-topic-digest
plan.title: Research topic digest
plan.description: Search the web for a topic, read the top articles, and compile key quotes from each into a notes file. Runs on demand when triggered.
plan.summary: Automates research by searching a topic online, extracting key quotes from the top results, and saving them to a persistent notes document.
plan.generalization: The recording shows one research run on "building better habits" with two articles. The automation generalizes this to accept a topic as input, search for it, read multiple top results (discovering URLs at runtime), extract one key quote from each article, and append them to a notes file. The topic and target file are fixed values; the article URLs are discovered by fetching and parsing the search results.

steps.label: Search the web for the topic
steps.prompt: Use web_fetch to search Google for articles on the topic '{{topic}}'. Fetch https://www.google.com/search?q={{topic}} (URL-encoded), parse the results to extract the URLs of the top 2–3 article links, and collect their full URLs for the next step.

steps.label: Read articles and extract key quotes
steps.prompt: For each article URL found: use web_fetch to read the article content. Identify and extract one key sentence or quote that captures the main insight. Store each quote with its source URL. Stop after collecting quotes from 2–3 articles.

steps.label: Append quotes to the notes file
steps.prompt: Open the notes file at {{notes_file}}. For each quote collected, append a line with the format 'Quote: [quote text] (Source: [URL])'. Save the file. If the file does not exist, create it first.

plan.name: reconcile-expense-charges
plan.title: Reconcile and file business trip expenses
plan.description: Reconcile each business-trip charge from the American Express statement against its receipt PDF, enter it in Expensify, and submit the expense report. Runs on demand or on a user-defined schedule (e.g., weekly or after a trip ends).
plan.summary: Match AmEx charges to receipt PDFs, file each as an expense in Expensify, and submit the report.
plan.generalization: The recording showed three specific charges (United, Marriott, Uber) being reconciled one by one. The automation generalizes this to iterate over ALL charges in the current AmEx statement: for each charge, locate and verify its matching receipt PDF, then file it in Expensify. Finally, submit the complete expense report. The shell and browser tools locate the files and statements dynamically instead of hard-coding the specific 2026 receipts or the three recorded amounts.

steps.label: Fetch and parse AmEx charges
steps.prompt: Open {{amex_activity_url}} using the browser, take a snapshot, and extract all recent business-trip charges (date, vendor, amount) from the page. Parse the charges into a structured list. Stop here and show the extracted charges for review before proceeding to reconciliation.

steps.label: Reconcile each charge against its receipt
steps.prompt: For each charge from the previous step, locate the matching receipt PDF in {{receipt_folder}} by vendor name and date. Open the receipt in Preview, confirm the amount matches the charge, and note that the charge is verified. If a receipt is missing, flag it and skip that charge. Collect the reconciled charges (vendor, amount, date) for filing.

steps.label: File reconciled expenses in Expensify
steps.prompt: Open {{expensify_base_url}}/expenses/new. For each reconciled charge, fill in the vendor name, amount, date, and category (Travel for airlines/hotels, Transportation for Uber/taxis), and attach the receipt PDF. Submit each expense. Continue until all reconciled charges are filed.

steps.label: Submit the expense report
steps.prompt: Navigate to {{expensify_base_url}}/reports. Review the filed expenses, ensure all reconciled charges are present, then submit the expense report. Confirm the submission succeeded (e.g., status changed to Submitted).

currentPlanIssues.message: Read local receipt files with view, not the Preview desktop UI.
Use view to read local receipt PDFs; mentioning a PDF or opening a viewer is not a native read tool.

plan.name: release-milestone-and-deploy
plan.title: Release a milestone to production
plan.description: Compile release notes from merged pull requests for a milestone into the CHANGELOG, bump the version, deploy to production, and verify the health endpoint.
plan.summary: Automates the release process: pulls main, gathers merged PRs for a named milestone, updates the CHANGELOG with PR titles, bumps the version, deploys to production, and confirms the health check passes.
plan.generalization: The recording compiled three specific PR titles for the v2.4.0 milestone. The generalized automation will iterate over ALL merged PRs for the specified milestone, extract their titles, append them to the CHANGELOG, then proceed with versioning and deployment. The core loop is: get all merged PRs → extract titles → update CHANGELOG once with all of them → deploy.

steps.label: Pull the latest main branch
steps.prompt: Run `git checkout main && git pull` to fetch and check out the latest main branch.

steps.label: Gather merged PRs for the milestone
steps.prompt: Use `gh pr list -R {{repo}} --search 'milestone:{{milestone}} is:merged' --json 'number,title'` to fetch all merged pull requests for the milestone. Extract the PR number and title from each and format as '#{number} {title}'.

steps.label: Update CHANGELOG with merged PR titles
steps.prompt: Read the {{changelog_file}} file, append each merged PR title (formatted as '#{number} {title}') to the appropriate section for the milestone, and save the updated file.

steps.label: Bump version and commit
steps.prompt: Run `npm version minor` to bump the version automatically, which creates a commit and a git tag for the new version.

steps.label: Deploy to production
steps.prompt: Execute the production deployment script using `{{deploy_script}} production` and wait for it to complete.

steps.label: Health-check the deployment
steps.prompt: Verify the deployment succeeded by fetching the health endpoint at {{health_endpoint}} using `curl -s {{health_endpoint}}` and confirming it returns a successful response (status 200).

plan.name: lead-to-crm
plan.title: Lead to CRM
plan.description: Qualify inbound sales leads from the mailbox by enriching each via LinkedIn, then create CRM contacts in Salesforce. Runs daily at 9am to process new lead emails.
plan.summary: Read new sales leads from the Sales Leads mailbox, look up each person on LinkedIn, and create a contact in Salesforce.
plan.generalization: The recording showed 2 leads processed from the Sales Leads inbox. The automation generalizes this to read all unread emails in the Sales Leads inbox (or a configurable lead source), enrich each via a LinkedIn public profile search, and create a corresponding contact in Salesforce CRM.

steps.label: Read inbound lead emails
steps.prompt: Use workiq_search_emails to find all unread emails in the {{mailbox}} mailbox folder. Extract the lead name, title, company, and email address from each message. Build a list of leads to process.

steps.label: Enrich each lead via LinkedIn
steps.prompt: For each lead name and company from the email list, use web_fetch to search for and read the person's public LinkedIn profile (construct the likely profile URL and fetch it). Capture their title, location, and any other enrichment details available.

steps.label: Create CRM contacts in Salesforce
steps.prompt: For each enriched lead, navigate to {{crm_instance}}/lightning/o/Contact/new using browser_navigate, use browser_snapshot to see the form, fill in the contact fields (first name, last name, title, company, email) using browser_fill_form or browser_type, and submit. Then create an opportunity linked to the contact if the lead indicates sales interest.
